scenes.say: Turned forty, and now you hold your phone at arm's length to read it? Meet Senthil.

scenes.en: Far is clear. Menus and messages up close are blurry.
scenes.say: Senthil is forty six. Far away, he sees perfectly. But menu cards and phone messages look blurry up close.

scenes.en: The lens inside your eye gets stiffer with age, so near focus gets hard.
scenes.say: Inside your eye is a flexible lens. To read up close, it changes shape. After about forty, it slowly gets stiffer, so near focus becomes hard. This is called presbyopia.

scenes.en: It happens to almost everyone after 40, even with perfect eyesight before.
scenes.say: Did you know? It happens to almost everyone after forty, even people who never needed glasses before. It is not a disease. It is a normal part of ageing.

scenes.en: Holding things far. Tired eyes after reading. Needing brighter light.
scenes.ta: தூரமாக பிடிப்பது, படித்த பின் கண் சோர்வு, அதிக வெளிச்சம் தேவை
scenes.say: Common signs: holding things far away, tired eyes or a headache after reading, and needing brighter light.

scenes.en: Skip readymade readers. Test each eye. Ask about progressive lenses.
scenes.ta: ரெடிமேட் கண்ணாடி வேண்டாம். முழு கண் பரிசோதனை செய்யுங்கள்
scenes.say: Don't just pick up readymade reading glasses. Each eye can need a different power. Get a full eye test, and ask about progressive lenses for near and far in one pair. If your vision changes suddenly, see an eye specialist the same day.
Senthil reads easily again. After forty, get your eyes tested every year. Book an eye test today.
